body:
Rule. First in, first out. Enqueue at the back, dequeue at the front. A deque softens the rule by allowing work at both ends without becoming a free-for-all middle edit.

Why it matters. Breadth-first search, scheduling fair work, and streaming buffers need arrival order. If you accidentally use a stack, the oldest request starves. Interviews listen for that fairness story.

SAMPLE example. SAMPLE: you walk a tree level by level. Seed the queue with the root. While it is not empty, take the front node, record its value, and enqueue its children. Nodes that arrived earlier leave earlier, so each level finishes before the next begins.

When to use. Pick a queue for BFS, for producer-consumer buffers, and for rate windows that expire the oldest event. Use a deque when sliding algorithms need to drop from the front while appending at the back.

When to refuse. Refuse a queue when the newest unfinished frame must resume first — use a stack. Refuse a naive array shift for dequeue if that shift is O(n) and the prompt expects amortized constant ends. Refuse conflating this structure with a system-design work queue topic; that sister slug is work-queues.
